answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, and hence paying the canyon bond on all of them and exposing each to the umber slash. Because the ridge audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 3 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Each impostor pays 17 dollars up front. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
